findings.current: in-force

findings.evidence: WebSearch: 'Regulation (EU) 2026/1738 ... on circularity requirements for vehicle design and on management of end-of-life vehicles repeals Directives 2000/53/EC and 2005/64/EC. The ... Regulation entered into force on 13 August 2026 ... general application occurring on 1 September 2028.' Exact repeal date not verified.

findings.current: Emissions
findings.proposed: none of the taxonomy systems fits well (end-of-life/recycling directive); 'Emissions' is misleading
findings.evidence: Repo summary: requirements for collection, treatment, recovery and recycling of end-of-life vehicles and hazardous-substance restrictions (Art 4), not emissions.

findings.current: Battery safety
findings.proposed: Environmental/waste directive (collection, recycling, hazardous substance limits, labelling); 'Battery safety' (vehicle traction-battery safety) is misleading - consider no system tag
findings.evidence: Repo summary: 'prohibits placing on the market batteries containing mercury or cadmium above set thresholds, and mandates high collection and recycling rates' - no safety/performance requirement.

findings.current: includes Emissions
findings.proposed: drop 'Emissions' (tyre rolling resistance/noise and safety systems; no exhaust-emission requirements in this act); 'Noise' and 'Tires & wheels' already cover it
findings.evidence: Repo body: Art 9 / Annex II cover tyre rolling resistance, wet grip and rolling noise; no pollutant emission limits.

findings.current: Passenger car, Light truck, Heavy truck, Trailer
findings.proposed: add Bus (and Motorcycle if L-category is deemed in scope - note: L-category is under Reg 168/2013, not 2018/858)
findings.evidence: 2018/858 covers M1-M3, N1-N3, O1-O4 incl. M2/M3 buses; 'Bus' is a taxonomy value and absent.

findings.current: Emissions, EV charging, Battery safety
findings.proposed: Emissions only
findings.evidence: Regulation sets fleet-average CO2 targets and ZLEV benchmarks (body Art 1 'Subject matter and objectives'); no EV charging or battery-safety requirements.

findings.current: UN R101
findings.proposed: none (fleet-level CO2 target regulation); R101 is only the underlying CO2/fuel consumption measurement method (M1 ICE/hybrid), alongside R154 for WLTP
findings.evidence: 2019/631 is a manufacturer fleet-average performance standard, not a vehicle type-approval technical requirement; UN R101 measures CO2/range for individual vehicles.
